observations: Line 2 uses a raw string prefix check `resolved.startswith(root)` rather than a path-component boundary check, so a sibling path sharing the root's prefix (e.g. '/srv/application/key' vs root '/srv/app') is accepted; probe p1 exercises exactly this case.
The contract states inputs are canonical absolute POSIX paths without symlinks or trailing slash, but line 2 performs no validation of that precondition, so the guarantee rests entirely on callers.
Line 2 returns a bool with no normalization or case handling; correctness depends on the stated canonicalization invariant holding for both arguments.
Line 1's signature `permitted(root, resolved)` accepts any two strings; there is no check that `root` is non-empty, so an empty root would make `startswith` true for every input.
The function is a pure predicate with no state, I/O, or exception paths; the only observable behavior is the boolean from line 2.
No authorization context (identity, role, or resource owner) is passed or consulted; the decision is purely path-based.
